recipes.name: Creamy Mashed Potatoes (Piure de Cartofi)
recipes.description: Fluffy potatoes beaten with warm milk and butter, finished with a whisper of nutmeg.
instructions: Peel the potatoes, cut them into even chunks and place in a pot of cold salted water.
Bring to a boil and simmer for 18-20 minutes until a knife slides in with no resistance.
Meanwhile warm the milk with the butter in a small pan until the butter melts.
Drain the potatoes well and let them steam dry in the pot for a minute.
Mash thoroughly, then beat in the warm milk and butter until smooth and fluffy.
Season with salt, white pepper and a pinch of nutmeg; serve hot.

recipes.name: Crispy Roast Potatoes with Rosemary
recipes.description: Parboiled, roughed-up potatoes roasted in hot oil until shatteringly crisp with garlic and rosemary.
instructions: Preheat the oven to 220°C and put a roasting tray with the oil inside to heat up.
Peel the potatoes, cut into large chunks and parboil in salted water for 8 minutes.
Drain and shake the colander hard to rough up the edges of each piece.
Carefully tip the potatoes into the hot oil and turn to coat.
Roast for 25 minutes, turn the potatoes, add the garlic cloves and rosemary, then roast 20 minutes more until deep golden.
Season generously with salt and pepper and serve immediately.

recipes.name: Baked Paprika Potato Wedges
recipes.description: Skin-on wedges tossed in olive oil, paprika and oregano, baked until crisp outside and fluffy inside.
instructions: Preheat the oven to 200°C and line a baking tray with baking paper.
Scrub the potatoes and cut each into 6-8 wedges, leaving the skin on.
Toss the wedges with olive oil, paprika, garlic powder, oregano, salt and pepper until evenly coated.
Spread in a single layer, skin side down where possible.
Bake for 30-35 minutes, turning once, until golden and crisp at the edges.

recipes.name: Hasselback Potatoes
recipes.description: Thinly sliced fan potatoes basted with garlic-thyme butter and crowned with crisp Parmesan.
instructions: Preheat the oven to 200°C.
Place each potato between two wooden spoon handles and slice thinly across, stopping before you cut through.
Melt the butter with the olive oil, crushed garlic and thyme leaves.
Set the potatoes in a baking dish, brush with half the butter and season with salt.
Bake for 30 minutes, brush with the remaining butter so it seeps between the slices, and bake 25 minutes more.
Scatter over the Parmesan and bake 5 more minutes until golden and crisp.

recipes.name: Potato Dauphinoise
recipes.description: Layers of thin potato slices baked slowly in garlic-infused cream under a golden Gruyère crust.
instructions: Preheat the oven to 160°C and butter a deep baking dish.
Peel the potatoes and slice them 3 mm thick with a mandoline or sharp knife.
Bring the cream, milk, crushed garlic, nutmeg, salt and white pepper to a simmer in a wide pan.
Add the potato slices and simmer gently for 10 minutes, stirring now and then so they do not stick.
Transfer to the dish, level the top and scatter over the grated cheese.
Bake for 60-65 minutes until the potatoes are tender and the top is deeply golden; rest 10 minutes before serving.

recipes.name: Cartofi Țărănești (Country-Style Potatoes with Smoked Bacon)
recipes.description: Romanian pan-fried potatoes with smoky bacon, onion, garlic and sweet paprika, finished with parsley.
instructions: Boil the potatoes in their skins for 15 minutes until just tender, then cool, peel and cut into thick slices.
Dice the bacon and fry it in the oil in a large pan over medium heat until the fat renders and it turns golden.
Add the chopped onion and cook for 5 minutes until soft.
Add the potato slices in a single layer and fry without stirring too often until browned on both sides.
Stir in the crushed garlic and paprika, cook for 1 minute, then season with salt and pepper.
Scatter with chopped parsley and serve hot.

recipes.name: Cartofi Natur cu Mărar (Buttered Potatoes with Dill)
recipes.description: Simple boiled potatoes tossed in melted butter and a generous handful of fresh dill.
instructions: Peel the potatoes and cut any large ones in half so they are all a similar size.
Cook in boiling salted water for 18-20 minutes until tender, then drain well.
Return the potatoes to the hot pot, add the butter and shake gently to coat.
Scatter over the chopped dill, season with salt and serve warm.

recipes.name: Crispy Sweet Potato Fries
recipes.description: Oven-baked sweet potato batons dusted with cornstarch and smoked paprika for extra crunch.
instructions: Preheat the oven to 220°C and line two baking trays with baking paper.
Peel the sweet potatoes and cut into 1 cm thick sticks; pat them very dry.
Toss with the cornstarch until lightly coated, then add the oil, smoked paprika, garlic powder and salt.
Spread out in a single layer with space between the fries.
Bake for 15 minutes, flip, and bake 12-15 minutes more until crisp at the edges; cool 5 minutes before serving.

recipes.name: Mămăligă (Romanian Polenta)
recipes.description: Golden cornmeal porridge stirred until thick, the classic Romanian partner for stews, cheese and sour cream.
instructions: Bring the water and salt to a rolling boil in a heavy pot.
Pour the cornmeal in a thin steady stream while whisking constantly to prevent lumps.
Reduce the heat to low and cook for 25-30 minutes, stirring often with a wooden spoon, until it pulls away from the sides.
Stir in the butter, then turn out onto a board or into a bowl.
Let it set for 2 minutes and cut into wedges with a string or knife.

recipes.name: Varză Călită (Romanian Braised Cabbage)
recipes.description: Shredded cabbage slowly braised with onion, tomato paste, thyme and dill until sweet and silky.
instructions: Remove the outer leaves and core from the cabbage, then shred it finely.
Soften the chopped onions in the oil in a large pot over medium heat for 8 minutes.
Add the cabbage in batches with a pinch of salt, stirring until it wilts enough to fit.
Stir in the tomato paste, thyme, dill and bay leaves, and add a splash of water.
Cover and braise over low heat for 45-50 minutes, stirring occasionally, until very tender and lightly caramelised.
Season with salt and plenty of black pepper before serving.

recipes.name: Fasole Bătută (Romanian White Bean Purée)
recipes.description: Smooth white bean purée beaten with garlic and oil, topped with sweet caramelised paprika onions.
instructions: Soak the beans overnight, then drain and boil in fresh water with the bay leaves for 60-90 minutes until very soft.
Drain, reserving a cup of the cooking liquid, and discard the bay leaves.
Blend the beans with the crushed garlic, half the oil and a little cooking liquid until smooth and creamy; season with salt.
Slice the onions thinly and fry slowly in the remaining oil for 15 minutes until golden and sweet.
Stir the paprika into the onions off the heat.
Spread the purée in a dish and spoon the paprika onions on top.

recipes.name: Mâncare de Spanac (Romanian Garlicky Spinach)
recipes.description: Wilted spinach bound in a light milk and flour sauce with plenty of garlic, a Romanian spring staple.
instructions: Wash the spinach well, blanch in boiling salted water for 1 minute, drain and chop roughly.
Soften the finely chopped onion in the oil over medium heat for 5 minutes.
Sprinkle in the flour and stir for 1 minute, then gradually whisk in the milk to make a smooth sauce.
Add the spinach and crushed garlic and simmer for 8-10 minutes, stirring, until thick.
Season with salt and pepper; serve warm, traditionally with a fried egg on top.

recipes.name: Murături Rapide (Quick Pickled Vegetables)
recipes.description: Crunchy cucumber, carrot and cauliflower in a sweet-sour brine with garlic and mustard seeds, ready in a day.
instructions: Cut the cucumbers into spears, the carrots into sticks and the cauliflower into small florets.
Pack the vegetables tightly into clean jars with the peeled garlic cloves and bay leaves.
Bring the water, vinegar, sugar, salt and mustard seeds to a boil, stirring to dissolve.
Pour the hot brine over the vegetables to cover them completely.
Seal, cool to room temperature and refrigerate for at least 24 hours before eating; keeps 2 weeks.

recipes.name: Sote de Ciuperci (Garlic Mushroom Sauté)
recipes.description: Mushrooms seared in butter until golden, then tossed with garlic and a shower of parsley.
instructions: Wipe the mushrooms clean and halve or quarter them depending on size.
Heat the oil and butter in a large pan over high heat until foaming.
Add the mushrooms in a single layer and leave undisturbed for 3 minutes so they brown, then stir and cook 5 minutes more.
Add the crushed garlic and cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Season with salt and pepper, stir in the chopped parsley and serve.

recipes.name: Dovlecei Pane (Breaded Fried Zucchini)
recipes.description: Zucchini rounds coated in flour, egg and breadcrumbs, fried golden and served with cool sour cream.
instructions: Slice the zucchini into 1 cm rounds, salt them lightly and leave 10 minutes, then pat dry.
Set up three plates: flour seasoned with salt and pepper, beaten eggs, and breadcrumbs.
Coat each slice in flour, dip in egg, then press into the breadcrumbs.
Heat the oil in a wide pan over medium heat and fry the slices in batches for 2-3 minutes per side until golden.
Drain on paper towels and serve warm with sour cream.

recipes.name: Conopidă Pane (Breaded Cauliflower)
recipes.description: Tender cauliflower florets in a crisp paprika breadcrumb crust, fried until golden brown.
instructions: Break the cauliflower into medium florets and boil in salted water for 5 minutes; drain and cool slightly.
Mix the breadcrumbs with the paprika; season the flour with salt and pepper; beat the eggs in a bowl.
Roll each floret in flour, dip in egg and coat well in the breadcrumbs.
Heat the oil in a deep pan over medium heat and fry the florets in batches for 3-4 minutes, turning, until golden.
Drain on paper towels, sprinkle with a little salt and serve hot.

recipes.name: Fasole Verde cu Usturoi (Green Beans with Garlic)
recipes.description: Blanched green beans tossed with raw garlic, oil, dill and a splash of vinegar, served warm or cold.
instructions: Trim the green beans and cook in boiling salted water for 6-8 minutes until tender but still bright.
Drain and rinse briefly under cold water to stop the cooking.
Crush the garlic with a pinch of salt and whisk with the oil and vinegar.
Toss the warm beans with the garlic dressing and the chopped dill.
Taste for salt and serve warm or at room temperature.

recipes.name: Mazăre Sote (Buttered Peas with Dill)
recipes.description: Sweet green peas simmered briefly with soft onion and butter, finished with fresh dill.
instructions: Melt the butter in a saucepan and soften the finely chopped onion for 5 minutes without browning.
Add the peas and the broth, bring to a simmer and cook for 6-8 minutes until the peas are tender.
Let most of the liquid bubble away so the peas are glossy, not soupy.
Season with salt and pepper and stir in the chopped dill just before serving.

recipes.name: Zacuscă de Casă (Roasted Eggplant and Pepper Spread)
recipes.description: Slow-cooked spread of roasted eggplant, kapia peppers and onion in tomato, Romania's autumn pantry classic.
instructions: Roast the eggplants and peppers over a flame or under a hot grill until the skins are blackened; cover and let steam 15 minutes.
Peel both, drain the eggplants well and chop everything finely.
Cook the finely chopped onions in the oil in a large heavy pot over medium heat for 15 minutes until soft and golden.
Add the peppers, eggplant, tomato paste, bay leaves, sugar, salt and pepper.
Simmer uncovered over low heat for 60-90 minutes, stirring often, until thick and the oil rises to the surface.
Remove the bay leaves, spoon into sterilised jars and seal while hot.

recipes.name: Honey-Roasted Carrots with Thyme
recipes.description: Whole carrots roasted until caramelised at the edges in honey, olive oil and fresh thyme.
instructions: Preheat the oven to 200°C.
Peel the carrots and halve lengthways any that are thick so they cook evenly.
Toss with the olive oil, honey, thyme leaves, salt and pepper on a baking tray.
Roast for 25-30 minutes, turning halfway, until tender and sticky at the edges.

recipes.name: Roasted Broccoli with Garlic and Lemon
recipes.description: High-heat roasted broccoli with crispy charred tips, sliced garlic, chili flakes and lemon zest.
instructions: Preheat the oven to 220°C.
Cut the broccoli into even florets and toss with the olive oil, sliced garlic, chili flakes and salt.
Spread on a baking tray in a single layer, cut sides down.
Roast for 18-20 minutes until the edges are crisp and lightly charred.
Grate over the lemon zest, squeeze over the juice and serve.

recipes.name: Spiced Roasted Cauliflower
recipes.description: Cauliflower florets roasted in cumin, turmeric and smoked paprika until golden, finished with lemon and parsley.
instructions: Preheat the oven to 210°C.
Cut the cauliflower into bite-sized florets.
Mix the olive oil with the cumin, turmeric, smoked paprika and salt, and toss the florets in it until well coated.
Spread on a baking tray and roast for 25-30 minutes, turning once, until golden and tender with crisp edges.
Squeeze over the lemon juice and scatter with chopped parsley.

recipes.name: Grilled Zucchini with Mint and Lemon
recipes.description: Charred zucchini ribbons dressed with olive oil, lemon, garlic and torn fresh mint.
instructions: Slice the zucchini lengthways into 5 mm ribbons and brush lightly with a little of the olive oil.
Heat a grill pan over high heat and grill the slices for 2-3 minutes per side until marked and tender.
Whisk the remaining olive oil with the lemon juice, finely grated garlic, salt and pepper.
Layer the warm zucchini on a platter, spoon over the dressing and scatter with torn mint leaves.
Rest 10 minutes to let the flavours soak in before serving.

recipes.name: Roasted Beetroot with Balsamic and Walnuts
recipes.description: Sweet roasted beetroot wedges glazed in balsamic vinegar and thyme, topped with toasted walnuts.
instructions: Preheat the oven to 200°C.
Peel the beetroot and cut into wedges; toss with the olive oil, thyme leaves, salt and pepper.
Spread on a baking tray, cover with foil and roast for 30 minutes.
Uncover, drizzle with the balsamic vinegar and roast 15-20 minutes more until tender and glossy.
Toast the walnuts in a dry pan for 3 minutes, chop roughly and scatter over the beetroot.

recipes.name: Roasted Pumpkin with Sage and Garlic
recipes.description: Caramelised pumpkin chunks roasted with whole garlic cloves and crisp sage, finished with pumpkin seeds.
instructions: Preheat the oven to 200°C.
Cut the pumpkin into 3 cm chunks, leaving the skin on if it is thin.
Toss with the olive oil, unpeeled garlic cloves, salt and pepper and spread on a baking tray.
Roast for 25 minutes, then add the sage leaves and pumpkin seeds and roast 8-10 minutes more until the pumpkin is tender and the sage crisp.
Squeeze the soft garlic from its skins over the pumpkin before serving.

recipes.name: Roasted Brussels Sprouts with Bacon
recipes.description: Halved sprouts roasted with bacon until crisp and caramelised, finished with a drizzle of balsamic glaze.
instructions: Preheat the oven to 210°C.
Trim the sprouts, halve them and toss with the olive oil, salt and pepper.
Spread cut side down on a baking tray and scatter over the chopped bacon.
Roast for 25-30 minutes, shaking the tray once, until the sprouts are browned and the bacon is crisp.
Drizzle with balsamic glaze and serve hot.

recipes.name: Braised Red Cabbage with Apples
recipes.description: Sweet-sour red cabbage slow-cooked with apple, cider vinegar, brown sugar and warm spices.
instructions: Quarter the cabbage, remove the core and shred finely; peel, core and dice the apples.
Melt the butter in a large pot and soften the sliced red onion for 5 minutes.
Add the cabbage, apples, vinegar, brown sugar, cloves, bay leaf and a good pinch of salt; stir well.
Cover and cook over low heat for 60-75 minutes, stirring occasionally, until the cabbage is very tender.
Remove the cloves and bay leaf, taste and adjust with more salt or vinegar.

recipes.name: Steakhouse Creamed Spinach
recipes.description: Rich spinach folded into a nutmeg-scented cream sauce with Parmesan, the classic steak companion.
instructions: Wilt the spinach in a large pan over high heat, drain in a colander and squeeze out as much liquid as possible; chop roughly.
Melt the butter in the same pan, add the crushed garlic and cook 1 minute.
Stir in the flour and cook for 1 minute, then whisk in the milk and cream until smooth and thickened.
Add the spinach, Parmesan and nutmeg and heat through for 3-4 minutes.
Season with salt and pepper and serve hot.

recipes.name: Brown Sugar Glazed Carrots
recipes.description: Stovetop carrot coins simmered in butter and brown sugar until glossy, with a scatter of parsley.
instructions: Peel the carrots and slice into 1 cm coins.
Put the carrots, butter, brown sugar, water and a pinch of salt in a wide pan.
Bring to a boil, cover and simmer for 8 minutes until almost tender.
Uncover and cook over high heat for 5-6 minutes, shaking the pan, until the liquid reduces to a shiny glaze.
Sprinkle with chopped parsley and serve.

recipes.name: Cheesy Garlic Bread
recipes.description: A baguette slathered with garlic-parsley butter and Parmesan, baked until crunchy and golden.
instructions: Preheat the oven to 200°C.
Mash the softened butter with the crushed garlic, chopped parsley, Parmesan and a pinch of salt.
Cut the baguette into thick slices without cutting all the way through the base.
Spread the garlic butter generously between the slices and over the top.
Wrap loosely in foil and bake for 10 minutes, then open the foil and bake 5 minutes more until crisp.

recipes.name: Yorkshire Puddings
recipes.description: Tall, crisp, hollow batter puddings baked in smoking-hot oil, essential alongside a roast and gravy.
instructions: Whisk the flour, eggs, milk and salt into a smooth batter and rest it for at least 30 minutes.
Preheat the oven to 230°C and pour a little oil into each cup of a 12-hole muffin tin.
Heat the tin in the oven for 10 minutes until the oil is smoking hot.
Quickly pour the batter into the cups, filling each about halfway, and return to the oven immediately.
Bake for 20-25 minutes without opening the door until puffed, deep golden and crisp; serve at once.

recipes.name: Corn on the Cob with Chili-Lime Butter
recipes.description: Sweet corn cobs boiled or grilled and rolled in zesty chili-lime butter with fresh coriander.
instructions: Mash the softened butter with the lime zest, lime juice, chili powder and salt.
Husk the corn and boil in unsalted water for 8-10 minutes, or grill over high heat for 10 minutes, turning, until charred in spots.
Spread the chili-lime butter over the hot cobs so it melts and coats them.
Scatter with chopped coriander and serve with extra lime wedges.

recipes.name: Homemade Smoky Baked Beans
recipes.description: White beans simmered in a smoky, tangy tomato sauce with brown sugar and mustard, far better than the tin.
instructions: Soften the finely chopped onion in the olive oil in a saucepan over medium heat for 6 minutes, then add the garlic for 1 minute.
Stir in the tomato sauce, brown sugar, mustard, smoked paprika and vinegar and bring to a simmer.
Drain and rinse the beans and add them to the sauce.
Simmer gently, uncovered, for 25-30 minutes, stirring now and then, until thick and glossy.
Season with salt and serve hot on toast or alongside eggs and sausages.

recipes.name: Crispy Polenta Fries with Parmesan
recipes.description: Set polenta cut into batons and baked until golden and crunchy, dusted with Parmesan and rosemary.
instructions: Bring the water and salt to a boil and whisk in the cornmeal; cook over low heat for 25 minutes, stirring often.
Beat in the butter and half the Parmesan, then spread 2 cm thick in an oiled tray and chill for at least 1 hour until firm.
Preheat the oven to 220°C and line a baking tray with baking paper.
Cut the set polenta into thick fries, brush with olive oil and sprinkle with rosemary.
Bake for 30-35 minutes, turning once, until golden and crisp; toss with the remaining Parmesan before serving.

recipes.name: Crispy Onion Rings
recipes.description: Thick onion rings in a crunchy paprika breadcrumb coating, deep-fried until golden brown.
instructions: Peel the onions, slice into 1 cm rings and separate them.
Set up three bowls: flour mixed with paprika and salt, eggs beaten with the milk, and breadcrumbs.
Dust each ring in flour, dip in the egg mixture, then coat in breadcrumbs, pressing to stick.
Heat the oil in a deep pan to 180°C and fry the rings in batches for 2-3 minutes until golden.
Drain on paper towels, sprinkle with salt and serve hot.

recipes.name: Caramelised Onions
recipes.description: Onions cooked low and slow in butter until deeply golden and jammy, finished with balsamic and thyme.
instructions: Peel and thinly slice the onions.
Heat the butter and olive oil in a wide heavy pan over medium-low heat and add the onions with the salt.
Cook for 35-40 minutes, stirring every few minutes and scraping the bottom, until soft and deep golden brown.
Stir in the brown sugar, balsamic vinegar and thyme leaves and cook 5 minutes more until sticky.
Serve warm, or cool and keep refrigerated for up to a week.

recipes.name: Creamy Cauliflower Mash
recipes.description: Silky low-carb mash of steamed cauliflower blended with garlic, cream cheese and Parmesan.
instructions: Cut the cauliflower into florets and steam or boil with the garlic cloves for 12-15 minutes until very tender.
Drain thoroughly and let it sit in the colander for 2 minutes so excess water evaporates.
Blend the cauliflower and garlic with the butter, cream cheese and Parmesan until smooth.
Season with salt and white pepper and serve hot.

recipes.name: Green Beans Almondine
recipes.description: Crisp-tender green beans tossed in nutty browned butter with toasted almonds, shallot and lemon.
instructions: Trim the beans and cook in boiling salted water for 5 minutes until crisp-tender; drain and refresh in cold water.
Melt the butter in a large pan over medium heat and toast the almonds for 2-3 minutes until golden.
Add the finely chopped shallot and cook for 1 minute.
Add the beans and toss for 2 minutes until hot and coated in butter.
Squeeze over the lemon juice, season with salt and pepper and serve.

recipes.name: Minted Pea Purée
recipes.description: Bright green pea purée blitzed with butter, fresh mint, a splash of cream and lemon.
instructions: Cook the peas in boiling salted water for 3-4 minutes until tender, then drain.
Blend the hot peas with the butter, mint leaves and cream until smooth, leaving a little texture if you like.
Add a squeeze of lemon juice and season with salt and pepper.
Return to the pan to warm through gently before serving.

recipes.name: Sage and Onion Stuffing
recipes.description: Buttery bread stuffing with soft onion, celery and fresh sage, baked until crisp on top and moist inside.
instructions: Preheat the oven to 180°C and butter a baking dish.
Tear the bread into small pieces and spread on a tray to dry out for 10 minutes in the oven.
Melt the butter in a pan and cook the chopped onions and celery for 8-10 minutes until soft.
Toss the bread with the onion mixture, chopped sage and parsley, salt and pepper.
Beat the egg into the broth, pour over the bread and mix gently until everything is moistened.
Spoon into the dish and bake for 35-40 minutes until golden and crisp on top.
